human_translations.translator_1: Three years went by swiftly, and the Patriarch again mounted his throne to lecture to the multitude. He discussed the scholastic deliberations and parables, and he discoursed on the integument of external conduct. Suddenly he asked, “Where’s Wukong?” Wukong drew near and knelt down. “Your pupil’s here,” he said. “What sort of art have you been practicing lately?” the Patriarch asked. “Recently,” Wukong said, “your pupil has begun to apprehend the nature of all things and my foundational knowledge has become firmly established.” “If you have penetrated to the dharma nature to apprehend the origin,” said the Patriarch, “you have, in fact, entered into the divine substance. You need, however, to guard against the danger of three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, he thought for a long time and said, “The words of the master must be erroneous. I have frequently heard that when one is learned in the Way and excels in virtue, he will enjoy the same age as Heaven; fire and water cannot harm him and every kind of disease will vanish. How can there be this danger of three calamities?” “What you have learned,” said the Patriarch, “is no ordinary magic: you have stolen the creative powers of Heaven and Earth and invaded the dark mysteries of the sun and moon. Your success in perfecting the elixir is something that the gods and the demons cannot countenance. Though your appearance will be preserved and your age lengthened, after five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of thunder to strike you. Hence you must be intelligent and wise enough to avoid it ahead of time. If you can escape it, your age will indeed equal that of Heaven; if not, your life will thus be finished. After another five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of fire to burn you. That fire is neither natural nor common fire; its name is the Fire of Yin, and it arises from within the soles of your feet to reach even the cavity of your heart, reducing your entrails to ashes and your limbs to utter ruin. The arduous labor of a millennium will then have been made completely superfluous. After another five hundred years the calamity of wind will be sent to blow at you. It is not the wind from the north, south, east, or west; nor is it one of the winds of four seasons; nor is it the wind of flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos. It is called the Mighty Wind, and it enters from the top of the skull into the body, passes through the midriff, and penetrates the nine apertures.12 The bones and the flesh will be dissolved and the body itself will disintegrate. You must therefore avoid all three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, his hairs stood on end, and, kowtowing reverently, he said, “I beg the master to be merciful and impart to me the method to avoid the three calamities. To the very end, I shall never forget your gracious favor.” The Patriarch said, “It is not, in fact, difficult, except that I cannot teach you because you are somewhat different from other people.” “I have a round head pointing to Heaven,” said Wukong, “and square feet walking on Earth. Similarly, I have nine apertures and four limbs, entrails and cavities. In what way am I different from other people?” The Patriarch said, “Though you resemble a man, you have much less jowl.” The monkey, you see, has an angular face with hollow cheeks and a pointed mouth. Stretching his hand to feel himself, Wukong laughed and said, “The master does not know how to balance matters! Though I have much less jowl than human beings, I have my pouch, which may certainly be considered a compensation.” “Very well, then,” said the Patriarch, “what method of escape would you like to learn? There is the Art of the Heavenly Ladle, which numbers thirty-six transformations, and there is the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which numbers seventy-two transformations.” Wukong said, “Your pupil is always eager to catch more fishes, so I’ll learn the Art of the Earthly Multitude.” “In that case,” said the Patriarch, “come up here, and I’ll pass on the oral formulas to you.” He then whispered something into his ear, though we do not know what sort of wondrous secrets he spoke of. But this Monkey King was someone who, knowing one thing, could understand a hundred! He immediately learned the oral formulas and, after working at them and practicing them himself, he mastered all seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_2: The Seeker of Secrets, having learnt the three secrets of Immortality: mind and spirit and abstinence from sex, memorized these carefully, and went on studying alone for three years more. Then the Master again mounted the platform and preached on the Parable of the Great Judgment. Suddenly he asked, “Where is the Seeker of Secrets?” The Monkey King came forward, knelt and said, “I am here.” The Master asked, “What have you been learning all this time?” “Your disciple has mastered the study of the spiritual nature.” The Master said, “Then you know the origin of things. But you must be careful of three great dangers.” The Seeker of Secrets, after pondering over this for a long time said, “I have constantly heard it said that when one has found Truth and Virtue, then one becomes an Immortal and no sickness can befall him; how then do you speak of dangers to be avoided?” The Master said, “What I teach you is not an ordinary doctrine, for it controls the forces of Heaven and Earth and the secrets of the sun, moon, and stars. When one has arrived at this stage, then one is superior to the evil spirits and the ordinary gods. Still after a time there will come a thunderclap to try your soul and spirit. If unmoved and unshaken in the deluge, you will be like Heaven itself. If you doubt, then you perish. After a long practice of religion again, one is tried a second time. This danger does not come from Heaven, nor from man, but from one’s own passions. It burns one’s whole body to ashes, and all one’s long years of practice are in vain like a dream. After another long term of practice, one is tried a third time by the danger of environment, which blows on one like a typhoon and affects one’s whole being. This must be overcome.” When the Seeker of Secrets heard this his body shook and his hair stood on end. “Oh Master, have pity on me, and tell me how to overcome these three dangers, and I shall never forget your kindness.” The Master said, “That is not difficult. There are two ways to avoid them. One has 36 wonders, the other 72; which do you wish to know?” The Seeker of Secrets said, “I wish to know the 72 wonders.” “Come here then, and I will teach you the incantation.” Then he whispered it in his ear. The Monkey King felt influences going through every pore of his body, and began to practice the arts and to learn the whole 72 wonders.
human_translations.translator_3: Another three years passed before Subodhi reappeared to teach his disciples. He spoke of academic debates and parables and of external self-cultivation. “Where’s Monkey?” he suddenly asked. Monkey kneeled before him. “Here I am!” “What have you been working on of late?” “The basics of immortality: the nature and origins of all things.” “In that case, you have already penetrated the divine substance of matter. But beware of the peril of the three calamities.” Monkey mulled this over for a while. “Master is surely mistaken,” he eventually responded. “I thought that anyone who has learned the Way and is rich in virtue will live as long as Heaven itself. Neither fire, nor water, nor illness can harm him. What three calamities do you speak of?” “What you have learned is not ordinary magic. You have stolen the creative power of heaven and earth itself, and penetrated the dark formulae of the sun and the moon. Ghosts and spirits will seek to bring you down. Although you have extended your life, in five hundred years’ time Heaven will unleash the calamity of thunder at you. You must seek wisdom to prevent this peril. Succeed and you will live as long as Heaven itself. Fail and you will die. In another five hundred years, Heaven will rain the calamity of the cold, dark fire of yin. It burns from the soles of your feet to the cavity of your heart. It will reduce your entrails to ashes and your limbs to ruins. Your millennium of hard work will then be as dust and nothingness. After another five hundred years, Heaven will set the calamity of wind onto you. This is no earthly wind. It enters through the fontanels, blows through the six internal organs, midriff, and nine orifices. Your flesh and bones will dissolve and your body will disintegrate. You see, then, why I recommend avoiding these calamities.” Monkey’s fur stood on end. “Tell me how to escape these horrors!” “Normally, this would be perfectly simple. But as you are an unusual specimen, I fear I cannot teach you.” “I’ve a head at the top and feet at the bottom, nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six internal organs. How am I unusual?” “You bear a superficial resemblance to humans, but your cheeks are abnormally flat.” (Monkeys have rather angular faces, with sunken cheeks and pointed muzzles.) Monkey patted his face combatively. “Appearances can be deceptive. My cheek pouches have storage capacity on the inside. I demand parity.” “Fair enough,” considered Subodhi. “Which escape do you want to learn? There’s the Art of the Big Dipper, which involves thirty-six transformations, or the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which involves seventy-two.” “The more the merrier,” considered Monkey. “I’ll take the second.” “Come over here, then, and I will tell you the formula.” No one knows what Subodhi whispered into Monkey’s ear. But our hero was someone who could learn a hundred things from a single explanation. He immediately memorized the magic and, after practicing on his own, mastered the seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? The Monkey King was the sort of person who understands everything once he is told a tiny part, and he learned the spells on the spot. He practiced and trained until he had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

translation: It had been three years since the Old Master had ascended to his throne again and preached to the multitude, using parables and discussing the external form. Suddenly, he asked, "Where is the Awakened Monkey?" The Awakened Monkey came forward, kneeling down, and said, "I am your disciple." The Old Master asked, "What kind of doctrine have you been practicing lately?" The Awakened Monkey replied, "I have recently made progress in my understanding of the true nature and have also solidified my foundation." The Old Master said, "If you have achieved understanding of the true nature and mastered the source, why do you still worry about the three calamities and their misfortunes?" The Awakened Monkey pondered this for a long time and said, "Master's words are incorrect. I have always heard that the Way is elevated and virtuous, coequal with Heaven, and when the yin and yang have reached harmony, no sickness arises. So how can there be these three calamities and their misfortunes?" The Old Master said, "This is an extraordinary Way: it involves taking away Heaven and Earth's creative power and invading the subtle mechanisms of the sun and moon. After attaining enlightenment, it is difficult for ghosts and spirits to abide. Although you may maintain your youth and long life, after five hundred years, a thunder calamity will come and you must use your insight and wisdom to avoid it in advance. If you can avoid it, your life will be as long as Heaven's, but if you fail to avoid it, your life will come to an end. After another five hundred years, a fire calamity will descend and burn you. This fire is neither divine fire nor ordinary fire, and it is called '陰火' or 'dark fire'. It will arise from your 'mingmen' meridian, pass through the 'hudun' palace, burn the five viscera to ashes, and reduce your limbs to withered bones, rendering all your thousand-year efforts futile. After another five hundred years, a wind calamity will come and blow you away. This wind is neither an eastern, southern, western, or northern wind, nor a gentle breeze, nor a gentle wind from flowers and willows, and it is called '赑風' or 'bare wind'. It will blow into your crown, pass through the dantian, pierce the nine apertures, dissolve your bones and flesh, and finally cause your body to disintegrate. Therefore, you must avoid them all." When the Awakened Monkey heard this, his bones were chilled with fear, and he bowed his head, paying his respects, saying, "I implore you, Grand Old Man, to be compassionate and teach me the method to avoid the three calamities." The Old Master said, "This is not difficult, but since you are different from others, I have not been able to teach you." The Awakened Monkey said, "I too am round-headed and stand on the ground with square feet, just like other people. I have nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six bowels, how am I any different from others?" The Old Master said, "Although you look like other people, you are less cheeky." Indeed, the monkey had a concave face and a pointed nose. The Awakened Monkey chuckled and said, "Master hasn't quite counted you correctly! Although I may be less cheeky, I have an additional pouch in my cheek, which is more than what others have, and I can still narrowly escape, I suppose." The Old Master said, "That doesn't matter, but you still want to learn the usual methods? There are ninety-six stellar permutations, seventy-two earth prison transformations. You want to learn the seventy-two earth prison transformations, right?" The Awakened Monkey said, "I'm willing to explore and learn, let me learn one earth prison transformation." The Old Master said, "If you are this willing, come forward and I will teach you the incantation." The Old Master whispered some mysterious words into his ear, and the Awakened Monkey quickly absorbed and practiced them, finally mastering the seventy-two earth prison transformations.

human_translations.translator_2: The Seeker of Secrets, having learnt the three secrets of Immortality: mind and spirit and abstinence from sex, memorized these carefully, and went on studying alone for three years more. Then the Master again mounted the platform and preached on the Parable of the Great Judgment. Suddenly he asked, “Where is the Seeker of Secrets?” The Monkey King came forward, knelt and said, “I am here.” The Master asked, “What have you been learning all this time?” “Your disciple has mastered the study of the spiritual nature.” The Master said, “Then you know the origin of things. But you must be careful of three great dangers.” The Seeker of Secrets, after pondering over this for a long time said, “I have constantly heard it said that when one has found Truth and Virtue, then one becomes an Immortal and no sickness can befall him; how then do you speak of dangers to be avoided?” The Master said, “What I teach you is not an ordinary doctrine, for it controls the forces of Heaven and Earth and the secrets of the sun, moon, and stars. When one has arrived at this stage, then one is superior to the evil spirits and the ordinary gods. Still after a time there will come a thunderclap to try your soul and spirit. If unmoved and unshaken in the deluge, you will be like Heaven itself. If you doubt, then you perish. After a long practice of religion again, one is tried a second time. This danger does not come from Heaven, nor from man, but from one’s own passions. It burns one’s whole body to ashes, and all one’s long years of practice are in vain like a dream. After another long term of practice, one is tried a third time by the danger of environment, which blows on one like a typhoon and affects one’s whole being. This must be overcome.” When the Seeker of Secrets heard this his body shook and his hair stood on end. “Oh Master, have pity on me, and tell me how to overcome these three dangers, and I shall never forget your kindness.” The Master said, “That is not difficult. There are two ways to avoid them. One has 36 wonders, the other 72; which do you wish to know?” The Seeker of Secrets said, “I wish to know the 72 wonders.” “Come here then, and I will teach you the incantation.” Then he whispered it in his ear. The Monkey King felt influences going through every pore of his body, and began to practice the arts and to learn the whole 72 wonders.
human_translations.translator_3: Another three years passed before Subodhi reappeared to teach his disciples. He spoke of academic debates and parables and of external self-cultivation. “Where’s Monkey?” he suddenly asked. Monkey kneeled before him. “Here I am!” “What have you been working on of late?” “The basics of immortality: the nature and origins of all things.” “In that case, you have already penetrated the divine substance of matter. But beware of the peril of the three calamities.” Monkey mulled this over for a while. “Master is surely mistaken,” he eventually responded. “I thought that anyone who has learned the Way and is rich in virtue will live as long as Heaven itself. Neither fire, nor water, nor illness can harm him. What three calamities do you speak of?” “What you have learned is not ordinary magic. You have stolen the creative power of heaven and earth itself, and penetrated the dark formulae of the sun and the moon. Ghosts and spirits will seek to bring you down. Although you have extended your life, in five hundred years’ time Heaven will unleash the calamity of thunder at you. You must seek wisdom to prevent this peril. Succeed and you will live as long as Heaven itself. Fail and you will die. In another five hundred years, Heaven will rain the calamity of the cold, dark fire of yin. It burns from the soles of your feet to the cavity of your heart. It will reduce your entrails to ashes and your limbs to ruins. Your millennium of hard work will then be as dust and nothingness. After another five hundred years, Heaven will set the calamity of wind onto you. This is no earthly wind. It enters through the fontanels, blows through the six internal organs, midriff, and nine orifices. Your flesh and bones will dissolve and your body will disintegrate. You see, then, why I recommend avoiding these calamities.” Monkey’s fur stood on end. “Tell me how to escape these horrors!” “Normally, this would be perfectly simple. But as you are an unusual specimen, I fear I cannot teach you.” “I’ve a head at the top and feet at the bottom, nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six internal organs. How am I unusual?” “You bear a superficial resemblance to humans, but your cheeks are abnormally flat.” (Monkeys have rather angular faces, with sunken cheeks and pointed muzzles.) Monkey patted his face combatively. “Appearances can be deceptive. My cheek pouches have storage capacity on the inside. I demand parity.” “Fair enough,” considered Subodhi. “Which escape do you want to learn? There’s the Art of the Big Dipper, which involves thirty-six transformations, or the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which involves seventy-two.” “The more the merrier,” considered Monkey. “I’ll take the second.” “Come over here, then, and I will tell you the formula.” No one knows what Subodhi whispered into Monkey’s ear. But our hero was someone who could learn a hundred things from a single explanation. He immediately memorized the magic and, after practicing on his own, mastered the seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? The Monkey King was the sort of person who understands everything once he is told a tiny part, and he learned the spells on the spot. He practiced and trained until he had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

translation:
Not long after, the Patriarch once again occupied his seat, and the assembly listened as he explained the principles of the doctrine. Using an analogy, he was discussing the process of cultivating the "flesh skin" outside the body. Just then, he inquired: "Where is the Monkey?"

The Monkey stepped forward and knelt down, saying: "I am your disciple."

The Patriarch asked: "You have been cultivating the Way, what has your spiritual practice been?"

The Monkey replied: "My spiritual nature has become clear, and my roots have grown deep."

The Patriarch said: "If your spiritual nature is clear, and you've mastered your roots, you've already obtained the divine body. However, you must beware of the three calamities."

The Monkey listened attentively and pondered for a long time before responding: "Father's words are mistaken. I often hear it said that a sage is lofty and venerable, and his lifespan equals the heavens; his yin and yang are harmonious, and all illnesses are eradicated. How could there be three calamities?"

The Patriarch replied: "This is a superior and rare type of cultivation. It involves stealing the creative power of heaven and earth, and violating the subtle essence of the sun and moon. Even though you may attain immortality, after five hundred years, the heavenly forces will bring down a calamity to strike you, requiring you to see your true nature and cultivate your wisdom to avoid it in advance. If you can avoid it, your lifespan will equal that of the heavens; if not, you will die at that time. Five hundred years later, a fire calamity will come to ravage you. This is not ordinary fire, nor is it mundane fire; it's called the 'dark fire.' It will rise up from the 'fountainhead' below your navel, pass through the palace of the Muddy Pellet, reduce your five organs to ashes, and rot your four limbs, rendering all your hard work in the past thousand years an illusion. Another five hundred years will pass, and the wind calamity will blow. This is not the wind from the east, south, west, or north, nor is it the wind of the grain-harvesting or the frost's chill; it's called the 'Descending Wind.' It will blow into your brain cavity, pass through your elixir field, and pierce your nine orifices, dissolving your bones and muscles, so that your body will be disintegrated. Therefore, you must avoid all three calamities."

The Monkey listened and his very bones were chilled to the marrow. He bowed his head in respect, saying: "Great-grandfather has compassionately imparted the method to avoid the calamities; I shall not forget this great debt."

The Patriarch said: "This is no difficult matter. It's just that you are different from others, so you cannot be taught."

The Monkey said: "I too, have a round head reaching to the heavens, feet that are square, capable of standing on the earth, and possess the nine orifices, four limbs, five organs, and six viscera, just like ordinary people. How am I any different?"

The Patriarch replied: "Although you appear human, you have fewer facial whiskers."

In fact, the Monkey had a small chin and a pointed mouth. The Monkey reached out to feel his face, laughing and saying: "Father has made a mistake! Although I may have fewer whiskers, I have this special pouch; it's quite useful, don't you think?"

The Patriarch said: "Fine, you want to learn from ordinary people? There are 36 heavenly stars, which correspond to 36 different transformations, and 72 terrestrial stars, corresponding to 72 different transformations."

The Monkey said: "I would like to deeply understand, let me learn one type of terrestrial star transformation."

The Patriarch said: "Since you're so eager, come forward and I'll teach you the oral formula."

He whispered into the Monkey's ear, but the Monkey didn't know what wise method he spoke. At that moment, the Monkey had suddenly understood all the mysteries and was able to cultivate the 72 terrestrial star transformations; he spent a long time practicing and refining himself, and eventually mastered all of them.
source_text: 却早过了三年，祖师复登宝座，与众说法。谈的是公案比语，论的是外像包皮。忽问：“悟空何在？”悟空近前跪下：“弟子有。”祖师道：“你这一向修些什么道来？”悟空道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源亦渐坚固矣。”祖师道：“你既通法性，会得根源，已注神体，却只是防备着‘三灾利害’。”悟空听说，沉吟良久道：“师父之言谬矣。我常闻道高德隆，与天同寿，水火既济，百病不生，却怎么有个三灾利害？”祖师道：“此乃非常之道：夺天地之造化，侵日月之玄机；丹成之后，鬼神难容。虽驻颜益寿，但到了五百年后，天降雷灾打你，须要见性明心，预先躲避。躲得过，寿与天齐，躲不过，就此绝命。再五百年后，天降火灾烧你。这火不是天火，亦不是凡火，唤做‘阴火’。自本身涌泉穴下烧起，直透泥垣宫，五脏成灰，四肢皆朽，把千年苦行，俱为虚幻。再五百年，又降风灾吹你。这风不是东南西北风，不是和薰金朔风，亦不是花柳松竹风，唤做‘赑风’。自囟门中吹入六腑，过丹田，穿九窍，骨肉消疏，其身自解。所以都要躲过。”悟空闻说，毛骨悚然，叩头礼拜道：“万老爷垂悯，传与躲避三灾之法，到底不敢忘恩。”祖师道：“此亦无难，只是你比他人不同，故传不得。”悟空道：“我也头圆顶天，足方履地，一般有九窍四肢，五脏六腑，何以比人不同？”祖师道：“你虽然像人，却比人少腮。”原来那猴子孤拐面，凹脸尖嘴。悟空伸手一摸，笑道：“师父没成算！我虽少腮，却比人多这个素袋，亦可准折过也。”祖师说：“也罢，你要学那一般？有一般天罡数，该三十六般变化，有一般地煞数，该七十二般变化。”悟空道：“弟子愿多里捞摸，学一个地煞变化罢。”祖师道：“既如此，上前来，传与你口诀。”遂附耳低言，不知说了些甚么妙法。这猴王也是一窍通时百窍通，当时习了口诀，自修自炼，将七十二般变化，都学成了。

human_translations.translator_4: After three years had passed in this way the Patriarch once more sat on his lecturing throne and expounded the Dharma to the students. He recounted famous sayings and parables, and discussed external phenomena and external appearances. Without warning he asked, “Where is Sun Wukong?” Sun Wukong went forward, knelt down and replied, “Your disciple is present.” “What Way have you cultivated since coming here?” “Your disciple is now fairly well conversant with the Dharma,” Sun Wukong replied, “and my Source is getting gradually stronger.” “If you are conversant with the Dharma and you know about the Source,” the Patriarch replied, “and if the spirit has already flowed into you, then you must beware of the 'Three Disasters.'” Sun Wukong thought for a long time, then he said, “Patriarch, you're talking rubbish. I have often heard that the Way is lofty and its power mighty, that it is as eternal as Heaven, that it can overcome fire and water, and prevent all illnesses from arising, so how could there be “Three Disasters?'” To this the Patriarch replied, “This is not the ordinary Way: it involves seizing the very creation of Heaven and Earth, and encroaching on the hidden workings of the sun and moon. Once the elixir is made, devils and spirits cannot tolerate it. Although it will preserve the youthfulness of your face and prolong your life, in five hundred years' time Heaven will strike you with a thunderbolt. You must be clear-sighted in nature and mind, so that you can hide from it before it comes. If you succeed in avoiding it you will live as long as Heaven; and if you don't, it will kill you. Another five hundred years later Heaven will burn you with fire. This fire will be not heavenly fire or ordinary fire but 'hidden fire'. It will burn you from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head; your five viscera will be reduced to ashes, your four limbs will be destroyed, and a thousand years of asceticism will have been so much wasted time. Yet another five hundred years later a wind will blow at you. It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? translation: Three years had passed, the Patriarch ascended to the throne again and preached to the assembly. His teaching focused on subtle affairs, analyzing the external appearance and inner reality. Suddenly, he asked, "Where is the Monkey King?" The Monkey King approached, bowing down: "Your disciple is here." The Patriarch asked, "What has your disciple been cultivating?" The Monkey King replied, "My recent practice has gained a deeper understanding of the Buddha-nature, and my root is gradually solidified." The Patriarch said, "If you have attained the Buddha-nature and grasped the root, yet still have the Buddha-body divine energy (qi), then why do you need to guard against 'Three Calamities'?" The Monkey King listened and pondered for a long time before saying, "Your words are wrong, venerable master. I often heard that a Great Sage cultivates virtue that matches the heavens and lives forever, and that water and fire are harmonized, resulting in no illness. Why would there be 'Three Calamities'?" The Patriarch said, "This is an extraordinary path: stealing heaven and earth's creative power, invading the celestial mechanism of the sun and moon. After becoming a dan, the gods and spirits find it difficult to bear. Although one maintains a youthful appearance and longevity, after five hundred years, a thunder disaster will be sent from heaven, and you must see your true nature and illuminate your mind beforehand to avoid it. If you can avoid it, you will live in harmony with heaven, but if not, you will die. Five hundred years later, a fire disaster will be sent, which is neither divine fire nor ordinary fire, called 'Dark Fire'. From the spring well (jīn qióng shuǐ) at the base of the spine, it will rise up and pierce the mud palace, reducing the five viscera to ash, and making the four limbs rotten. Another five hundred years later, a disaster of 'chaotic wind' (fàn fēng) will blow. This is not the wind of the eight directions, nor is it the gentle breeze of the golden sun or the fragrant wind of flowers and trees, but is called 'chaotic wind'. From the fontanelle (wú dé róu) at the top of the head, it will blow into the six cavities, passing through the nine orifices, and dissipate the bones and flesh. Thus, it's necessary to avoid all three calamities." The Monkey King listened, and his bones felt cold with fright, prostrating himself in reverence and bowing down, saying, "The Venerable Lord shows pity, transmitting the method to avoid the Three Calamities. I will never forget your benevolence." The Patriarch said, "This is no difficult matter; the reason you cannot receive the transmission is that you are unlike others." The Monkey King said, "I also have a head that reaches the sky and feet that cover the earth, just like ordinary people, with nine apertures and four limbs, five viscera and six cavities, what makes me different from them?" The Patriarch said, "Although you are similar to people, you have fewer facial whiskers." The Monkey King stretched out his hand to feel, laughed and said, "Venerable Master, you've under-estimated! I may have fewer whiskers, but I have this forehead bag (qī tóu xiū dài), and it's enough to allow me to transform." The Patriarch said, "Very well, then you should learn the general transformations, of which there are thirty-six types, or the specific talismans, of which there are seventy-two types." The Monkey King said, "I wish to delve deeper and study one type of transformation, let's say, a specific talisman." The Patriarch said, "Since you're willing to do so, come forward and I'll transmit the secret manual to you." So the Patriarch whispered in his ear, saying something wondrous, and at the time, the Monkey King was enlightened to all aspects and mastered the hundred transformations. The Monkey King then studied and practiced the secret, mastering all seventy-two transformations.
source_text: 却早过了三年，祖师复登宝座，与众说法。谈的是公案比语，论的是外像包皮。忽问：“悟空何在？”悟空近前跪下：“弟子有。”祖师道：“你这一向修些什么道来？”悟空道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源亦渐坚固矣。”祖师道：“你既通法性，会得根源，已注神体，却只是防备着‘三灾利害’。”悟空听说，沉吟良久道：“师父之言谬矣。我常闻道高德隆，与天同寿，水火既济，百病不生，却怎么有个三灾利害？”祖师道：“此乃非常之道：夺天地之造化，侵日月之玄机；丹成之后，鬼神难容。虽驻颜益寿，但到了五百年后，天降雷灾打你，须要见性明心，预先躲避。躲得过，寿与天齐，躲不过，就此绝命。再五百年后，天降火灾烧你。这火不是天火，亦不是凡火，唤做‘阴火’。自本身涌泉穴下烧起，直透泥垣宫，五脏成灰，四肢皆朽，把千年苦行，俱为虚幻。再五百年，又降风灾吹你。这风不是东南西北风，不是和薰金朔风，亦不是花柳松竹风，唤做‘赑风’。自囟门中吹入六腑，过丹田，穿九窍，骨肉消疏，其身自解。所以都要躲过。”悟空闻说，毛骨悚然，叩头礼拜道：“万老爷垂悯，传与躲避三灾之法，到底不敢忘恩。”祖师道：“此亦无难，只是你比他人不同，故传不得。”悟空道：“我也头圆顶天，足方履地，一般有九窍四肢，五脏六腑，何以比人不同？”祖师道：“你虽然像人，却比人少腮。”原来那猴子孤拐面，凹脸尖嘴。悟空伸手一摸，笑道：“师父没成算！我虽少腮，却比人多这个素袋，亦可准折过也。”祖师说：“也罢，你要学那一般？有一般天罡数，该三十六般变化，有一般地煞数，该七十二般变化。”悟空道：“弟子愿多里捞摸，学一个地煞变化罢。”祖师道：“既如此，上前来，传与你口诀。”遂附耳低言，不知说了些甚么妙法。这猴王也是一窍通时百窍通，当时习了口诀，自修自炼，将七十二般变化，都学成了。

He discussed the scholastic deliberations and parables, and he discoursed on the integument of external conduct. Suddenly he asked, “Where’s Wukong?” Wukong drew near and knelt down. “Your pupil’s here,” he said. “What sort of art have you been practicing lately?” the Patriarch asked. “Recently,” Wukong said, “your pupil has begun to apprehend the nature of all things and my foundational knowledge has become firmly established.” “If you have penetrated to the dharma nature to apprehend the origin,” said the Patriarch, “you have, in fact, entered into the divine substance. You need, however, to guard against the danger of three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, he thought for a long time and said, “The words of the master must be erroneous. I have frequently heard that when one is learned in the Way and excels in virtue, he will enjoy the same age as Heaven; fire and water cannot harm him and every kind of disease will vanish. How can there be this danger of three calamities?” “What you have learned,” said the Patriarch, “is no ordinary magic: you have stolen the creative powers of Heaven and Earth and invaded the dark mysteries of the sun and moon. But this Monkey King was someone who, knowing one thing, could understand a hundred! He immediately learned the oral formulas and, after working at them and practicing them himself, he mastered all seventy-two transformations.

It will not be the North, South, East, or West wind, nor will it be a warm, fragrant wind from the Northwest; nor will it be the kind of wind that blows among flowers, willows, pine, and bamboo. It will be what is called a 'monster wind'. It will blow through the crown of your head down into your six entrails. It will go through the Cinnabar Field below your navel and penetrate your nine orifices. Your flesh and your bones will be destroyed and your body will disintegrate. So you must avoid all three of these disasters.” When he heard this Sun Wukong's hair stood on end, and he kowtowed with the words, “I implore you, my lord, to show pity and teach me how to avoid these three disasters. If you do I will be grateful to you for ever.” “That would be easy,” the Patriarch replied, “but for the fact that you are different from other people—which means that I can't.” “I have a head that faces the sky and feet standing on earth,” said Sun Wukong. “I have nine orifices and four limbs, five viscera and six entrails. How am I different from anyone else?” “Although you are quite like other people, your cheeks are too small.” Now the Monkey had a funny face, with cheeks that caved inwards and a sharp chin. Sun Wukong felt it with his hand and replied with a laugh, “Master, you didn't take everything into account. Although I'm a bit short of jaw, I've got more dewlap than other people to make up for it.” “Very well then,” the Patriarch said, “which would you prefer to learn: the thirty-six heavenly transformations or the seventy-two earthly ones?” “Your disciple wants to get as much out of it as he can, so I would like to learn the seventy-two earthly ones.” “If that's what you want,” the Patriarch replied, “come here and I'll teach you the spells.” Thereupon he whispered into Sun Wukong's ear, and who knows what miraculous spells he taught him? The Monkey King was the sort of person who understands everything once he is told a tiny part, and he learned the spells on the spot. He practiced and trained until he had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

translation: But after three years had passed, the Venerable Master returned to his throne and taught the scriptures. His lecture was about analogies and cases, and he discussed the essence of one's external form. Suddenly he asked, "Where is the Monkey?" The Monkey drew near and bowed: "Your disciple is here." The Venerable Master said, "What practices have you been cultivating these days?" The Monkey replied, "Your disciple has recently achieved a relatively thorough understanding of the true nature, and his roots have become relatively firm." The Venerable Master said, "Since you have attained the true nature and understood the roots, you have already achieved enlightenment, yet you still need to be mindful of the 'three calamities that bring harm'." The Monkey listened and pondered for a long time before saying, "Your words are wrong, Master. I have often heard that one who cultivates the Way is endowed with great virtue and lives as long as heaven and earth, and when water and fire have been harmonized, there is no illness, so how can there be three calamities that bring harm?" The Venerable Master said, "This is an extraordinary doctrine: by seizing the creative power of heaven and earth and intruding upon the subtle mechanism of the sun and moon, one can attain the state of enlightenment. However, after one has transformed and perfected oneself, even the spirits will find it difficult to bear. Although one's appearance remains youthful and one's life is prolonged, after five hundred years, heaven will send a thunderstorm to strike you, and you must be able to see your true nature and wise heart beforehand and avoid it in time. If you avoid it, your lifespan will match that of heaven, but if you fail to avoid it, you will meet your demise. Five hundred years later, heaven will send a fire to burn you. This is not the fire of heaven or ordinary fire; it is called 'yin fire.' It begins to burn from the spring of life at the base of one's spine and penetrates through the eight palaces, causing the five viscera to turn to ashes and the four limbs to rot, reducing one's thousand years of ascetic practices to nothing but an illusion. Five hundred years later, heaven will send a gale to blow you. This is not the east wind, south wind, west wind, or north wind, nor is it the gentle autumn breeze or the spring breeze; it is called the 'burying wind.' It will blow from the fontanelle and enter the six cavities, passing through the elixir field and piercing the nine orifices, causing the body to disintegrate and the flesh and bones to scatter, and thus one's body will dissolve. Therefore, one must avoid all three calamities." The Monkey listened and was filled with terror, and he bowed his head and kowtowed, saying, "Wan Gao, may you show mercy and transmit to me the method of avoiding the three calamities, so that I will never forget your kindness." The Venerable Master said, "This is not difficult, but you are different from others, so you cannot learn it." The Monkey said, "I also have a round head that touches the heavens and feet that are square and plant-like, and I have nine orifices, four limbs, five viscera, and six cavities, so how am I different from others?" The Venerable Master said, "You may resemble others in appearance, but you have fewer cheekbones." The Monkey had a protruding face and a pointed chin, and he touched his cheek and said with a smile, "Master, you are mistaken! Although I have fewer cheekbones, I have this 'treasure bag' that is larger than humans, and it is enough for me to practice and perfect it as well." The Venerable Master said, "Well then, you want to learn one of the ordinary transformations, not the extraordinary ones? There are thirty-six Heavenly generals and seventy-two Earthly evil spirits, each with their own transformations." The Monkey said, "I want to learn the transformations of the Earthly evil spirits." The Venerable Master said, "Since that is the case, come closer and I will transmit to you the incantation." He then leaned in close and whispered some profound teachings, but I do not know what they were. This Monkey King became enlightened in an instant and, at that time, learned the incantation and practiced it, thus mastering all seventy-two transformations.
source_text: 却早过了三年，祖师复登宝座，与众说法。谈的是公案比语，论的是外像包皮。忽问：“悟空何在？”悟空近前跪下：“弟子有。”祖师道：“你这一向修些什么道来？”悟空道：“弟子近来法性颇通，根源亦渐坚固矣。”祖师道：“你既通法性，会得根源，已注神体，却只是防备着‘三灾利害’。”悟空听说，沉吟良久道：“师父之言谬矣。我常闻道高德隆，与天同寿，水火既济，百病不生，却怎么有个三灾利害？”祖师道：“此乃非常之道：夺天地之造化，侵日月之玄机；丹成之后，鬼神难容。虽驻颜益寿，但到了五百年后，天降雷灾打你，须要见性明心，预先躲避。躲得过，寿与天齐，躲不过，就此绝命。再五百年后，天降火灾烧你。这火不是天火，亦不是凡火，唤做‘阴火’。自本身涌泉穴下烧起，直透泥垣宫，五脏成灰，四肢皆朽，把千年苦行，俱为虚幻。再五百年，又降风灾吹你。这风不是东南西北风，不是和薰金朔风，亦不是花柳松竹风，唤做‘赑风’。自囟门中吹入六腑，过丹田，穿九窍，骨肉消疏，其身自解。所以都要躲过。”悟空闻说，毛骨悚然，叩头礼拜道：“万老爷垂悯，传与躲避三灾之法，到底不敢忘恩。”祖师道：“此亦无难，只是你比他人不同，故传不得。”悟空道：“我也头圆顶天，足方履地，一般有九窍四肢，五脏六腑，何以比人不同？”祖师道：“你虽然像人，却比人少腮。”原来那猴子孤拐面，凹脸尖嘴。悟空伸手一摸，笑道：“师父没成算！我虽少腮，却比人多这个素袋，亦可准折过也。”祖师说：“也罢，你要学那一般？有一般天罡数，该三十六般变化，有一般地煞数，该七十二般变化。”悟空道：“弟子愿多里捞摸，学一个地煞变化罢。”祖师道：“既如此，上前来，传与你口诀。”遂附耳低言，不知说了些甚么妙法。这猴王也是一窍通时百窍通，当时习了口诀，自修自炼，将七十二般变化，都学成了。

human_translations.translator_1: Three years went by swiftly, and the Patriarch again mounted his throne to lecture to the multitude. He discussed the scholastic deliberations and parables, and he discoursed on the integument of external conduct. Suddenly he asked, “Where’s Wukong?” Wukong drew near and knelt down. “Your pupil’s here,” he said. “What sort of art have you been practicing lately?” the Patriarch asked. “Recently,” Wukong said, “your pupil has begun to apprehend the nature of all things and my foundational knowledge has become firmly established.” “If you have penetrated to the dharma nature to apprehend the origin,” said the Patriarch, “you have, in fact, entered into the divine substance. You need, however, to guard against the danger of three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, he thought for a long time and said, “The words of the master must be erroneous. I have frequently heard that when one is learned in the Way and excels in virtue, he will enjoy the same age as Heaven; fire and water cannot harm him and every kind of disease will vanish. How can there be this danger of three calamities?” “What you have learned,” said the Patriarch, “is no ordinary magic: you have stolen the creative powers of Heaven and Earth and invaded the dark mysteries of the sun and moon. Your success in perfecting the elixir is something that the gods and the demons cannot countenance. Though your appearance will be preserved and your age lengthened, after five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of thunder to strike you. Hence you must be intelligent and wise enough to avoid it ahead of time. If you can escape it, your age will indeed equal that of Heaven; if not, your life will thus be finished. After another five hundred years Heaven will send down the calamity of fire to burn you. That fire is neither natural nor common fire; its name is the Fire of Yin, and it arises from within the soles of your feet to reach even the cavity of your heart, reducing your entrails to ashes and your limbs to utter ruin. The arduous labor of a millennium will then have been made completely superfluous. After another five hundred years the calamity of wind will be sent to blow at you. It is not the wind from the north, south, east, or west; nor is it one of the winds of four seasons; nor is it the wind of flowers, willows, pines, and bamboos. It is called the Mighty Wind, and it enters from the top of the skull into the body, passes through the midriff, and penetrates the nine apertures.12 The bones and the flesh will be dissolved and the body itself will disintegrate. You must therefore avoid all three calamities.” When Wukong heard this, his hairs stood on end, and, kowtowing reverently, he said, “I beg the master to be merciful and impart to me the method to avoid the three calamities. To the very end, I shall never forget your gracious favor.” The Patriarch said, “It is not, in fact, difficult, except that I cannot teach you because you are somewhat different from other people.” “I have a round head pointing to Heaven,” said Wukong, “and square feet walking on Earth. Similarly, I have nine apertures and four limbs, entrails and cavities. In what way am I different from other people?” The Patriarch said, “Though you resemble a man, you have much less jowl.” The monkey, you see, has an angular face with hollow cheeks and a pointed mouth. Stretching his hand to feel himself, Wukong laughed and said, “The master does not know how to balance matters! Though I have much less jowl than human beings, I have my pouch, which may certainly be considered a compensation.” “Very well, then,” said the Patriarch, “what method of escape would you like to learn? There is the Art of the Heavenly Ladle, which numbers thirty-six transformations, and there is the Art of the Earthly Multitude, which numbers seventy-two transformations.” Wukong said, “Your pupil is always eager to catch more fishes, so I’ll learn the Art of the Earthly Multitude.” “In that case,” said the Patriarch, “come up here, and I’ll pass on the oral formulas to you.” He then whispered something into his ear, though we do not know what sort of wondrous secrets he spoke of. But this Monkey King was someone who, knowing one thing, could understand a hundred! He immediately learned the oral formulas and, after working at them and practicing them himself, he mastered all seventy-two transformations.
human_translations.translator_2: The Seeker of Secrets, having learnt the three secrets of Immortality: mind and spirit and abstinence from sex, memorized these carefully, and went on studying alone for three years more. Then the Master again mounted the platform and preached on the Parable of the Great Judgment. Suddenly he asked, “Where is the Seeker of Secrets?” The Monkey King came forward, knelt and said, “I am here.” The Master asked, “What have you been learning all this time?” “Your disciple has mastered the study of the spiritual nature.” The Master said, “Then you know the origin of things. But you must be careful of three great dangers.” The Seeker of Secrets, after pondering over this for a long time said, “I have constantly heard it said that when one has found Truth and Virtue, then one becomes an Immortal and no sickness can befall him; how then do you speak of dangers to be avoided?” The Master said, “What I teach you is not an ordinary doctrine, for it controls the forces of Heaven and Earth and the secrets of the sun, moon, and stars. When one has arrived at this stage, then one is superior to the evil spirits and the ordinary gods. Still after a time there will come a thunderclap to try your soul and spirit. If unmoved and unshaken in the deluge, you will be like Heaven itself. If you doubt, then you perish. After a long practice of religion again, one is tried a second time. This danger does not come from Heaven, nor from man, but from one’s own passions. It burns one’s whole body to ashes, and all one’s long years of practice are in vain like a dream. After another long term of practice, one is tried a third time by the danger of environment, which blows on one like a typhoon and affects one’s whole being. This must be overcome.” When the Seeker of Secrets heard this his body shook and his hair stood on end. “Oh Master, have pity on me, and tell me how to overcome these three dangers, and I shall never forget your kindness.” The Master said, “That is not difficult. There are two ways to avoid them. One has 36 wonders, the other 72; which do you wish to know?” The Seeker of Secrets said, “I wish to know the 72 wonders.” “Come here then, and I will teach you the incantation.” Then he whispered it in his ear. The Monkey King felt influences going through every pore of his body, and began to practice the arts and to learn the whole 72 wonders.
human_translations.translator_3: Another three years passed before Subodhi reappeared to teach his disciples. He spoke of academic debates and parables and of external self-cultivation. “Where’s Monkey?” he suddenly asked. Monkey kneeled before him. “Here I am!” “What have you been working on of late?” “The basics of immortality: the nature and origins of all things.” “In that case, you have already penetrated the divine substance of matter. But beware of the peril of the three calamities.” Monkey mulled this over for a while. “Master is surely mistaken,” he eventually responded. “I thought that anyone who has learned the Way and is rich in virtue will live as long as Heaven itself. Neither fire, nor water, nor illness can harm him. What three calamities do you speak of?” “What you have learned is not ordinary magic. You have stolen the creative power of heaven and earth itself, and penetrated the dark formulae of the sun and the moon. Ghosts and spirits will seek to bring you down. Although you have extended your life, in five hundred years’ time Heaven will unleash the calamity of thunder at you. You must seek wisdom to prevent this peril. Succeed and you will live as long as Heaven itself. Fail and you will die. In another five hundred years, Heaven will rain the calamity of the cold, dark fire of yin. It burns from the soles of your feet to the cavity of your heart. It will reduce your entrails to ashes and your limbs to ruins. Your millennium of hard work will then be as dust and nothingness. After another five hundred years, Heaven will set the calamity of wind onto you. This is no earthly wind. It enters through the fontanels, blows through the six internal organs, midriff, and nine orifices. Your flesh and bones will dissolve and your body will disintegrate. You see, then, why I recommend avoiding these calamities.” Monkey’s fur stood on end. “Tell me how to escape these horrors!” “Normally, this would be perfectly simple. But as you are an unusual specimen, I fear I cannot teach you.” “I’ve a head at the top and feet at the bottom, nine apertures, four limbs, five viscera, and six internal organs. How am I unusual?” “You bear a superficial resemblance to humans, but your cheeks are abnormally flat.” (Monkeys have rather angular faces, with sunken cheeks and pointed muzzles.) Monkey patted his face combatively. “Appearances can be deceptive. My cheek pouches have storage capacity on the inside. But our hero was someone who could learn a hundred things from a single explanation. He immediately memorized the magic and, after practicing on his own, mastered the seventy-two transformations.

translation: The Russian heart can distinguish a great man even in the enemy of his homeland. That is to say, I don't remember if I literally expressed myself that way... I was a child... but I think that's what I meant! Napoleon was taken aback, he thought and said to his suite: "I love the pride of this child! But if all Russians think like this child, then..." – he didn't finish and entered the palace. I immediately intervened in the suite and ran after him. The suite parted to let me through and looked at me as a favorite. But all of that only flashed by... I remember only that, entering the first hall, the Emperor suddenly stopped in front of the portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it thoughtfully for a long time, and finally said: "She was a great woman!" – and passed on. In two days, everyone already knew me in the palace and in the Kremlin, and they called me "le petit boyard". I only went home to sleep. At home, I almost went mad. Two days later, Napoleon's chamberlain, Baron de Bazancourt, who couldn't withstand the campaign, died. Napoleon remembered me; I was taken, led without explaining the matter, tried on the uniform of the deceased, a boy of twelve years old, and when I was brought to the Emperor in the uniform, he nodded at me with his head, and then announced to me that I was honored by his majesty's favor and was promoted to chamberlain of his majesty. I was happy, I indeed felt a warm sympathy for him... well, and apart from that, a brilliant uniform is a lot for a child... I went in a dark-green tailcoat, with long and narrow folds; gold buttons, red cuffs with gold embroidery, a high, standing, open collar with gold embroidery, embroidery on the folds; white tight-fitting trousers, a white silk waistcoat, silk stockings, buckled shoes... and during the Emperor's horseback ride, and if I participated in the suite, high boots. Although the situation was not brilliant and the enormous misfortunes were already being foreseen, etiquette was observed as much as possible, and even more punctually as the misfortunes were being foreseen.
source_text: «Русское сердце в состоянии даже в самом враге своего отечества отличить великого человека!». То есть, собственно, не помню, буквально ли я так выразился... я был ребенок... но смысл наверно был тот! Наполеон был поражен, он подумал и сказал своей свите: «Я люблю гордость этого ребенка! Но если все русские мыслят, как это дитя, то...» — он не договорил и вошел во дворец. Я тотчас же вмешался в свиту и побежал за ним. В свите уже расступались предо мной и смотрели на меня как на фаворита. Но всё это только мелькнуло... Помню только, что, войдя в первую залу, император вдруг остановился пред портретом императрицы Екатерины, долго, смотрел на него в задумчивости и наконец произнес: «Это была великая женщина!» — и прошел мимо. Чрез два дня меня все уже знали во дворце и в Кремле и звали «le petit boyard». Я только ночевать уходил домой. Дома чуть с ума не сошли. Еще чрез два дня умирает камер-паж Наполеона, барон де Базанкур, не вынесший похода. Наполеон вспомнил обо мне; меня взяли, привели, не объясняя дела, примерили на меня мундир покойного, мальчика лет двенадцати, и, когда уже привели меня в мундире к императору и он кивнул на меня головой, объявили мне, что я удостоен милостью и произведен в камер-пажи его величества. gt_translation: "The Russian heart is able to distinguish a great man even in the very enemy of his fatherland!" That is, in fact, I don’t remember whether I literally put it that way ... I was a child ... but the meaning must have been the same! Napoleon was amazed, he thought and said to his retinue: “I love the pride of this child! But if all Russians think like this child, then ... ”- he did not finish and entered the palace. I immediately intervened in the retinue and ran after him. The retinue already made way for me and looked at me as a favorite. But all this only flashed by... I only remember that, having entered the first hall, the emperor suddenly stopped in front of the portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it for a long time in thought, and finally said: “That was a great woman!” — and passed by. Two days later, everyone in the palace and the Kremlin already knew me and called me "le petit boyard." I just went home for the night. The houses went a little crazy. Two days later, Napoleon's chamber page, Baron de Bazancourt, dies, unable to endure the campaign. Napoleon remembered me; They took me, brought me, without explaining the matter, tried on me the uniform of the deceased, a boy of about twelve years old, and when they had already brought me in uniform to the emperor and he nodded his head at me, they announced to me that I was honored with mercy and promoted to his chamber-page majesty. I was glad, I really felt for him, and for a long time already, a warm sympathy ... well, and besides, you will agree, a brilliant uniform, which is a lot for a child ... I went around in a dark green tailcoat, with long and narrow tails; gold buttons, red piping on sleeves with gold embroidery, high, standing, open collar, embroidered with gold, sewing on coattails; tight-fitting white leggings, a white silk waistcoat, silk stockings, shoes with buckles ... and during the emperor's walks on horseback, and if I participated in the retinue, high over the knee boots. Although the situation was not brilliant and huge disasters were already foreseen, etiquette was observed as much as possible, and even more punctually, the more these disasters were foreseen.

I immediately mingled with his suite and ran after him. Members of his entourage parted to make way for me and treated me as their favourite. But all this was over in a flash… I merely remember that on entering the first hall, the Emperor stopped suddenly before a portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it for a long time, lost in thought, and at last pronounced, ‘A grand lady indeed!’ and passed on. Two days later everyone knew me in the Palace and Kremlin and called me ‘le petit boyard’. * I used to go home only at night. At home people nearly went wild. In another two days Napoleon’s chamber page Baron de Bazancourt died without making it through the campaign. Napoleon remembered me. I was summoned, brought in without a word of explanation, told to put on the uniform of the deceased, a lad of about twelve and, after I was brought before the Emperor in my new outfit and he had given me a nod, was told I had been specially favoured and elevated to His Majesty’s chamber page. I was delighted. I really felt a strong attraction for him from the start… well, and on top of that there was the splendid uniform which meant so much to a young lad… I wore a dark green tailcoat with long, narrow flaps, gold buttons, red cuffs, stitched with gold thread, a high, stiff, open, gold-embroidered collar, the flaps being similarly decorated, tight-fitting, white, chamois leather pantaloons, a white silk vest, silk stockings, shoes with buckles… and when the Emperor went out riding, and I was included in his suite, I wore a pair of high riding boots. Но если все русские мыслят, как это дитя, то...» — он не договорил и вошел во дворец. Я тотчас же вмешался в свиту и побежал за ним. В свите уже расступались предо мной и смотрели на меня как на фаворита. Но всё это только мелькнуло... Помню только, что, войдя в первую залу, император вдруг остановился пред портретом императрицы Екатерины, долго, смотрел на него в задумчивости и наконец произнес: «Это была великая женщина!» — и прошел мимо. Чрез два дня меня все уже знали во дворце и в Кремле и звали «le petit boyard». Я только ночевать уходил домой. Дома чуть с ума не сошли. Еще чрез два дня умирает камер-паж Наполеона, барон де Базанкур, не вынесший похода. Наполеон вспомнил обо мне; меня взяли, привели, не объясняя дела, примерили на меня мундир покойного, мальчика лет двенадцати, и, когда уже привели меня в мундире к императору и он кивнул на меня головой, объявили мне, что я удостоен милостью и произведен в камер-пажи его величества. Я был рад, я действительно чувствовал к нему, и давно уже, горячую симпатию... ну, и кроме того, согласитесь, блестящий мундир, что для ребенка составляет многое... Я ходил в темно-зеленом фраке, с длинными и узкими фалдами; золотые пуговицы, красные опушки на рукавах с золотым шитьем, высокий, стоячий, открытый воротник, шитый золотом, шитье на фалдах; белые лосинные панталоны в обтяжку, белый шелковый жилет, шелковые чулки, башмаки с пряжками... а во время прогулок императора на коне, и если я участвовал в свите, высокие ботфорты. Хотя положение было не блестящее и предчувствовались уже огромные бедствия, но этикет соблюдался по возможности, и даже тем пунктуальнее, чем сильнее предчувствовались эти бедствия.
gt_translation: "The Russian heart is able to distinguish a great man even in the very enemy of his fatherland!" That is, in fact, I don’t remember whether I literally put it that way ... I was a child ... but the meaning must have been the same! Napoleon was amazed, he thought and said to his retinue: “I love the pride of this child! But if all Russians think like this child, then ... ”- he did not finish and entered the palace. I immediately intervened in the retinue and ran after him. The retinue already made way for me and looked at me as a favorite. But all this only flashed by... I only remember that, having entered the first hall, the emperor suddenly stopped in front of the portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it for a long time in thought, and finally said: “That was a great woman!” — and passed by. Two days later, everyone in the palace and the Kremlin already knew me and called me "le petit boyard." I just went home for the night. The houses went a little crazy. Two days later, Napoleon's chamber page, Baron de Bazancourt, dies, unable to endure the campaign. Napoleon remembered me; They took me, brought me, without explaining the matter, tried on me the uniform of the deceased, a boy of about twelve years old, and when they had already brought me in uniform to the emperor and he nodded his head at me, they announced to me that I was honored with mercy and promoted to his chamber-page majesty. I was glad, I really felt for him, and for a long time already, a warm sympathy ... well, and besides, you will agree, a brilliant uniform, which is a lot for a child ... I went around in a dark green tailcoat, with long and narrow tails; gold buttons, red piping on sleeves with gold embroidery, high, standing, open collar, embroidered with gold, sewing on coattails; tight-fitting white leggings, a white silk waistcoat, silk stockings, shoes with buckles ... and during the emperor's walks on horseback, and if I participated in the retinue, high over the knee boots. Although the situation was not brilliant and huge disasters were already foreseen, etiquette was observed as much as possible, and even more punctually, the more these disasters were foreseen.

human_translations.translator_1: To this instant question, I gave an instant reply, ‘A Russian deep in his heart can recognize a great man!’ Actually, to be perfectly frank, I don’t recall if that was word for word what I said… I was too young… but that was the gist of it! Napoleon was astonished. He thought awhile and said to his suite. ‘I admire this boy’s pride! But if all Russians think like this lad, then…’ He did not finish and entered the Palace. I immediately mingled with his suite and ran after him. Members of his entourage parted to make way for me and treated me as their favourite. But all this was over in a flash… I merely remember that on entering the first hall, the Emperor stopped suddenly before a portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it for a long time, lost in thought, and at last pronounced, ‘A grand lady indeed!’ and passed on. Two days later everyone knew me in the Palace and Kremlin and called me ‘le petit boyard’. * I used to go home only at night. At home people nearly went wild. In another two days Napoleon’s chamber page Baron de Bazancourt died without making it through the campaign. Napoleon remembered me. I was summoned, brought in without a word of explanation, told to put on the uniform of the deceased, a lad of about twelve and, after I was brought before the Emperor in my new outfit and he had given me a nod, was told I had been specially favoured and elevated to His Majesty’s chamber page. I was delighted. I really felt a strong attraction for him from the start… well, and on top of that there was the splendid uniform which meant so much to a young lad… I wore a dark green tailcoat with long, narrow flaps, gold buttons, red cuffs, stitched with gold thread, a high, stiff, open, gold-embroidered collar, the flaps being similarly decorated, tight-fitting, white, chamois leather pantaloons, a white silk vest, silk stockings, shoes with buckles… and when the Emperor went out riding, and I was included in his suite, I wore a pair of high riding boots. Although the general situation was not brilliant to say the least and there was the whiff of enormous disaster in the air, etiquette was observed whenever possible and the more punctiliously, the closer disaster loomed.”

I was a child ... but that was probably the gist of it! Napoleon was struck, he thought for a moment and said to his retinue: “I like the pride of this boy! But if all Russians think like this child, then ...” He didn’t finish, and entered the palace. I at once joined the retinue and ran after him. The members of the retinue were already stepping aside for me and looking on me as a favourite. But all that just fleeted past ... I remember only that, as he entered the first hall, the emperor suddenly stopped in front of a portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it for a long time and, said, at last: “She was a great woman!” - and walked past. Two days later everyone in the palace and the Kremlin knew me, and called me “le petit boyard”. I only went home to sleep. At home they were almost beside themselves. Another two days later, Napoleon’s page, Baron de Bazancourt,5 died after failing to endure the campaign. Napoleon remembered me. I was taken and brought to the palace without explanation, was given the uniform of the deceased, a boy of about twelve, and when they had led me to the emperor, wearing the uniform, and he had nodded at me, they told me that I had been granted favour and been made a page of his majesty. I was pleased, I really did feel an ardent sympathy for him, and had done for a long time ... well, and also there was the resplendent uniform, which is something that means a great deal to a child ... I went about in a dark-green coat with long, narrow tails; gold buttons, red trimmings on the sleeves with gold braid, a high, stiff, open collar, embroidered in gold, embroidery on the tails; white, close-fitting buckskin breeches, silk stockings, shoes with buckles ... and during the emperor’s outings on horseback, and if I was part of the retinue, high hessian boots. Although the situation was none too good, and enormous calamities were already being anticipated, etiquette was observed as far as possible, and one could even say that it was observed with more punctilio the more strongly those calamities were sensed to be imminent.’

Two days later, I was already known throughout the palace and in the Kremlin, and they called me 'le petit boyard.' I only went home at night. At home, I almost went mad. Two days later, Napoleon's chamberlain, Baron de Bazancourt, died, unable to bear the march. Napoleon remembered me; I was taken, brought, without explaining the matter, and they tried me on the uniform of the deceased, a boy of twelve years old. When they brought me in uniform to the Emperor and he nodded at me, they announced that I was honored and promoted to the rank of chamberlain of his Majesty. I was happy; I indeed felt a warm sympathy for him... and, in addition, agree that a bright uniform is a lot for a child... I went about in a dark green tailcoat, with long and narrow tails; golden buttons, red cuffs with golden embroidery, a high, standing, open collar with gold embroidery, embroidery on the tails; white close-fitting trousers, a white silk waistcoat, silk stockings, boots with buckles... and during the Emperor's rides on horseback, and if I participated in the suite, high top boots. Although the position was not brilliant and great calamities were already felt to be impending, etiquette was observed as best as possible, and even more punctually, the more the calamities were felt to be impending."
source_text: «Русское сердце в состоянии даже в самом враге своего отечества отличить великого человека!». То есть, собственно, не помню, буквально ли я так выразился... я был ребенок... но смысл наверно был тот! Наполеон был поражен, он подумал и сказал своей свите: «Я люблю гордость этого ребенка! Но если все русские мыслят, как это дитя, то...» — он не договорил и вошел во дворец. Я тотчас же вмешался в свиту и побежал за ним. В свите уже расступались предо мной и смотрели на меня как на фаворита. Но всё это только мелькнуло... Помню только, что, войдя в первую залу, император вдруг остановился пред портретом императрицы Екатерины, долго, смотрел на него в задумчивости и наконец произнес: «Это была великая женщина!» — и прошел мимо. Чрез два дня меня все уже знали во дворце и в Кремле и звали «le petit boyard». Я только ночевать уходил домой. Дома чуть с ума не сошли. Еще чрез два дня умирает камер-паж Наполеона, барон де Базанкур, не вынесший похода. Наполеон вспомнил обо мне; меня взяли, привели, не объясняя дела, примерили на меня мундир покойного, мальчика лет двенадцати, и, когда уже привели меня в мундире к императору и он кивнул на меня головой, объявили мне, что я удостоен милостью и произведен в камер-пажи его величества. Я был рад, я действительно чувствовал к нему, и давно уже, горячую симпатию... ну, и кроме того, согласитесь, блестящий мундир, что для ребенка составляет многое... Я ходил в темно-зеленом фраке, с длинными и узкими фалдами; золотые пуговицы, красные опушки на рукавах с золотым шитьем, высокий, стоячий, открытый воротник, шитый золотом, шитье на фалдах; белые лосинные панталоны в обтяжку, белый шелковый жилет, шелковые чулки, башмаки с пряжками... а во время прогулок императора на коне, и если я участвовал в свите, высокие ботфорты. Хотя положение было не блестящее и предчувствовались уже огромные бедствия, но этикет соблюдался по возможности, и даже тем пунктуальнее, чем сильнее предчувствовались эти бедствия.

human_translations.translator_1: To this instant question, I gave an instant reply, ‘A Russian deep in his heart can recognize a great man!’ Actually, to be perfectly frank, I don’t recall if that was word for word what I said… I was too young… but that was the gist of it! Napoleon was astonished. He thought awhile and said to his suite. ‘I admire this boy’s pride! But if all Russians think like this lad, then…’ He did not finish and entered the Palace. I immediately mingled with his suite and ran after him. Members of his entourage parted to make way for me and treated me as their favourite. But all this was over in a flash… I merely remember that on entering the first hall, the Emperor stopped suddenly before a portrait of Empress Catherine, looked at it for a long time, lost in thought, and at last pronounced, ‘A grand lady indeed!’ and passed on. Two days later everyone knew me in the Palace and Kremlin and called me ‘le petit boyard’. * I used to go home only at night. At home people nearly went wild. In another two days Napoleon’s chamber page Baron de Bazancourt died without making it through the campaign. Napoleon remembered me. I was summoned, brought in without a word of explanation, told to put on the uniform of the deceased, a lad of about twelve and, after I was brought before the Emperor in my new outfit and he had given me a nod, was told I had been specially favoured and elevated to His Majesty’s chamber page. I was delighted. I really felt a strong attraction for him from the start… well, and on top of that there was the splendid uniform which meant so much to a young lad… I wore a dark green tailcoat with long, narrow flaps, gold buttons, red cuffs, stitched with gold thread, a high, stiff, open, gold-embroidered collar, the flaps being similarly decorated, tight-fitting, white, chamois leather pantaloons, a white silk vest, silk stockings, shoes with buckles… and when the Emperor went out riding, and I was included in his suite, I wore a pair of high riding boots. Although the general situation was not brilliant to say the least and there was the whiff of enormous disaster in the air, etiquette was observed whenever possible and the more punctiliously, the closer disaster loomed.”
